title: Coax and connectors
idea: Loss in coax turns into heat. It goes up with frequency and down with better cable: foam, then RG-213, then hardline. Keep water out, and use Type N above 400 MHz.

items: Power lost in a feed line
Foam has less loss per foot
RG-213 has less loss at a given frequency
Moisture. A UV-resistant jacket keeps sunlight from cracking it and letting water in

cards.t: Raising the frequency in the same cable
cards.why: Loss in coax increases as frequency goes up. The impedance doesn't change.
Foam-dielectric coax has less loss per foot.
RG-213 has less loss at a given frequency.

cards.t: Air-insulated hardline instead of flexible coax
cards.why: Air-insulated hardline has the lowest loss of all.
RG-58 is the lossier of the two.
Foam is the low-loss one, so solid loses more per foot.

cards.t: Lowering the frequency in the same cable
cards.why: Loss goes down as frequency goes down.

compare.how: Common at HF and VHF. Not watertight, not bayonet, not for microwaves.
Less loss at a given frequency.

traps.why: Feed line loss doesn't raise SWR. The lost power turns into heat.

traps.wrong: Operation at 100% duty cycle for an extended period
traps.why: Long transmissions don't wear out coax. Moisture getting in does.

traps.wrong: Ultraviolet light can increase losses in the cable’s jacket
traps.why: UV light cracks the jacket so water gets in. That's the problem, not jacket loss.

traps.wrong: It is more resistant to moisture contamination
traps.why: Foam's advantage is less loss per foot, not moisture resistance.
Amateur coax is most commonly 50 ohms.
The impedance stays the same. It's the loss that rises with frequency.
PL-259 is for HF and VHF. Above 400 MHz, use Type N.
PL-259 connectors aren't watertight. They're common at HF and VHF.

traps.wrong: RG-58 cable can handle higher power levels
traps.why: The difference is loss: RG-213 has less at a given frequency.
Any flexible coax loses more than air-insulated hardline.
